newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open listless, eye on Nippecraft.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open listless, eye on Nippecraft.

text.p: Singapore shares started on a lethargic note on Tuesday with dealers expecting the market to keep to a sideways trend.
"The market is quiet. Most people are expecting a sideways movement in Singapore," said a dealer at a local broking house.
At 0136 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index dipped 0.64 point to 2,176.52. Market volume was a meagre 9.5 million shares with 25 rises against 32 falls.
Dealers said they were watching diary maker Nippecraft which was attracting speculative interest. It was up Singapore S$0.025 to S$0.63 (US$0.45) on 1.11 million shares traded.
"We don't know what's going on. Usually it's a takeover story," said one remisier.

Several small block trades were reported in the morning. Among them were Hotel Properties with 100,000 shares crossed at S$2.21 and Roly International with 129,000 shares crossed at S$0.65. Malaysian over the counter stocks Kemayan saw a 1.5 million share block deal at S$1.976 and Technology Resources had 130,000 shares crossed at S$3.626.
Selected blue chips like Fraser & Neave, SIA foreign and DBS Bank foreign were slightly firmer on light volumes.
